frontier.hypothesis: With K38 and K39 closing both non-arithmetic escapes, the ONLY route to the target arrangement is H17's window insn_count in [120, 122] reached at zero emitted cost, and K40 says every known carrier for that window is dead at loop exit. The one term never independently re-derived from source is whether count_loop_regs_set's 'i'-class count can be inflated by insns that survive cse1 and loop but are merged away by a LATER pass (combine.c, flow.c, jump2) rather than by biv elimination.
frontier.mechanism: insn_count is computed by count_loop_regs_set before strength reduction (loop.c:3001-3092). s5's BYTE-COUNT COUPLING law claimed everything surviving loop_optimize also survives combine and reload, and s6 falsified it for ONE deletion path (biv elimination inside loop_optimize). combine.c runs after loop and merges 2-3 insn chains into one pattern, so a chain that cse1 cannot fold but combine can would be a second free-count channel that no session has tested.
frontier.next_probe: Build a sweep of k in {4, 8, 16, 32} in-loop combine-foldable chains whose value IS consumed by an existing store (so cse1's delete_dead_from_cse cannot remove them and s5's K15 harness does not apply) — e.g. widening/narrowing pairs on the u8 destination, or shift-add pairs feeding the existing sb — and read insn_count in the .loop dump against build_insns from sandbox. If insn_count rises while build_insns stays at 105 the channel is real and admissible; if build_insns tracks insn_count 1:1 the s5 coupling law holds for combine and the [120,122] window is carrier-empty for ordinary C.

frontier.hypothesis: The threshold halving at loop.c:532 (loop_has_call ? 1 : 2) is the only dial that changes the requirement by more than -3 per slot, and with a call in the loop the magic would decline at insn_count >= 59 instead of >= 120 — a +3 requirement instead of +64.
frontier.mechanism: threshold 61 for a loop containing a CALL_INSN; slot 1 moves at 61 >= c (needs c <= 61), then threshold 58 and the magic declines at c > 58. The window becomes [59, 61] — reachable by K36's free index bivs plus a handful of insns rather than by 64 of them.
frontier.next_probe: s8's K26 dismissed this as 'still hoists' using the wrong arithmetic (it compared 58 against insn_count 56 without adding the call's own in-loop insns). Measure it: put an existing-callee call inside the loop (the target has no jal in its loop, so this is diagnostic only) and read whether the .loop dump reports threshold-driven decline at insn_count in [59,61]. Even if byte-foreclosed, the measurement fixes the exact width of the window under loop_has_call and tells the next session whether any call-free construct sets loop_has_call (prescan_loop) — e.g. a libcall-expanded operation such as a 64-bit divide or a float op — which would be an ordinary-C handle on the same dial.

frontier.hypothesis: pb_array_subscript.c remains a byte-equivalent second chassis (15 / 105) whose pre-cse1 RTL differs from candidate.c, so any future permuter or solver campaign has two independent seeds.
frontier.mechanism: cse1 folds the array-subscript address arithmetic into the same givs the index-derived-pointer spelling produces, so the two bodies emit identical instructions while presenting different mutation neighbourhoods.
frontier.next_probe: If a permuter campaign is re-run (s4 ran 66,016 iterations on the pointer spelling with zero finds), seed it from tmp/grind/func_8003C714/s12/pb_array_subscript.c instead.
